**Governor Gavin Newsom’s plan to commute every death sentence in California — 548 in all — has drawn a sharp attack from President Donald Trump, who called the move a “disaster for Justice in America.”**

Newsom’s office has identified 548 intended recipients — 529 men and 19 women.

you.title: Trump blasts Newsom's 'shocking' death penalty commutations
you.snippet:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump blasted Gov. Gavin Newsom’s decision to commute every death sentence in California, calling the move “one of the most shocking acts of injustice our country has ever seen” at a Monday press conference with victims’ family members at the Department of Justice.
Trump said he “couldn’t believe” Newsom’s choice to commute the sentences of some of California’s most notorious serial killers and rapists. He used a good portion of the event to describe in great detail some of the murders that landed the 548 condemned people in California on death row, specifically mentioning Charles Ng, who was convicted of murdering nine adults and two children in 1984-85, Randy Kraft, a serial murderer known in the 1970s and ‘80s as the “Scorecard Killer” and Robert Boyd Rhoades, who brutally raped, tortured and killed 8-year-old Michael Lyons in 1996, among others.
